learningObjectives: Distinguish checkout ownership from use of an existing Module.
Use IF branches and bounded WHILE/DO loops.
Configure recovery and retry scope without duplicating setup.
Validate uniqueness for parent-scoped or wildcard identification.
Distinguish node counts, table cell counts and table dimensions.
Repeat folder steps while accounting for changing table indexes.

elements.text: Green checkout indicators mean you hold the object; red means another user holds it; white identifies a new object. Inspect checkout details rather than assuming every lock belongs to another person.

A Module held by another user cannot be edited by you, but its existing definition can still be referenced by your editable TestCases. Checkout is an editing coordination mechanism, not a guarantee of test readiness or success.

IF evaluates Conditions, then executes THEN when true or optional ELSE when false. It is not a loop. WHILE checks before its Loop and may run zero times; DO runs its Loop before checking and normally runs at least once.

WHILE and DO have MaximumRepetitions, default 30, to bound iteration. A false condition is control-flow information and does not itself fail the overall test. Bound polling and inspect what happens when the maximum is reached.

Independent practice: initialize a numeric buffer, evaluate it below a small limit and increment it in the loop. Use TBox Evaluation Tool for buffer conditions. This is not the verified Academy Exercise 23 procedure.

elements.text: Original Academy exercise 23 and its figures were inaccessible. This lesson supplies independent documentation-based guidance; no original exercise or Tosca run was performed.

Create Recovery Scenario Collections on TestCases or TestCase folders. Enable the relevant dialog, verification or exception failure handling through TBox Recovery settings, or override those settings with TCPs. ScratchBook does not support Recovery; exercise it through an ExecutionList.

RetryLevel chooses the failure granularity and the point of resumption: TestStepValue, TestStep or TestCase. It does not describe the object where the collection must be created. Successful Recovery retries from that level; repeating a whole case may duplicate setup or side effects.

When Recovery fails, CleanUp attempts to restore the environment for subsequent execution. It is not an always-run teardown for every passing case. Scenarios live in the collection and are tried in order with higher-level fallback.

NonGUI recovery does not support TestStepValue RetryLevel. Exception Recovery inside conditional statements is unsupported with TestStep/TestStepValue RetryLevel. Review these boundaries before designing retries.

Original Academy exercise 25 and its figures were inaccessible. This lesson supplies independent documentation-based guidance; no original exercise or Tosca run was performed.

With Verify, Order number: {XB[OrderNumber]} checks the static text while capturing the variable substring in buffer OrderNumber. Read it later with {B[OrderNumber]}; the bracket content is the buffer name, not a fixed expected order ID.

Start with stable, unique properties. If they cannot distinguish a control, select a stable parent before the child and validate uniqueness within that scope. A parent alone does not distinguish three identical child buttons; an additional stable discriminator or justified index is needed.

Changing IDs can use a wildcard for the variable suffix, provided the remaining criteria are unique. Positional indexes can become invalid when the UI changes. ExplicitName permits editing a TestStepValue name; it does not create a stable technical ID in the SUT.
Original Academy exercise 26 and its figures were inaccessible. This lesson supplies independent documentation-based guidance; no original exercise or Tosca run was performed.
Original Academy exercise 27 and its figures were inaccessible. This lesson supplies independent documentation-based guidance; no original exercise or Tosca run was performed.

ExplicitName=True on an XModuleAttribute allows editing its referenced XTestStepValue name; a semicolon-separated value range is another supported form. The meaning of names or # indexes depends on the control type. It is not a universal dynamic-ID repair.

TBox Set Buffer uses a named ModuleAttribute: Input writes the value, Verify checks an existing value. Dynamic expressions can supply values. It does not read the SUT merely because a buffer was named.

ResultCount has two contexts. A general control property counts matching current nodes, for example .ResultCount==5 with Verify. Table ResultCount counts constrained cells, excludes configured headers and needs table Select plus cell Constraint; row/column Verify limits scope. Choose the intended context.

For a table, RowCount and ColumnCount measure table dimensions. Inspect the actual header configuration and returned count before converting it to data-only counts; do not subtract one blindly when the table has no header. Buffer syntax uses a property arrow, for example RowCount->RowNum. Header-relative $ positions differ from absolute # positions.

Original Academy exercise 29 and its figures were inaccessible. This lesson supplies independent documentation-based guidance; no original exercise or Tosca run was performed.

For a known or dynamically evaluated non-negative count, use Repetition on a TestStepFolder, either in the Details column or Properties. It applies to folders inside a TestCase, not manual tests or parallel execution with AOS. {REPETITION} and {REPETITION[FolderName]} are documented expressions for checking repetition.

When removing rows, positions shift. Repeatedly remove the current first data row after verifying the count/state, or identify each target by a stable business key. Incrementing the row position after deleting earlier rows can skip items.

Constraint restricts the search for the parent row/node using child values. Require unique matching business values or a deliberate index among matches. Then use the correct action on an embedded Remove checkbox/control. Select navigates to nodes, Verify checks values and WaitOn waits within a timeout; they serve different purposes.

examPitfalls.title: Retry scope
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Choose RetryLevel deliberately to avoid duplicate setup/side effects.

examPitfalls.title: Conditional loops
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating a false loop condition as test failure.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Conditions guide branches; loops must be bounded.

examPitfalls.title: XBuffer purpose
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Verify static context and capture the variable substring.

examPitfalls.title: Buffer name
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Putting expected data in XB brackets.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: XB brackets name the captured buffer.

examPitfalls.title: Constraint uniqueness
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming matching values are automatically unique.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect uniqueness or use a deliberate matching index.

examPitfalls.title: Repeat scope
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Repeating the full entry instead of its folder steps.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use TestStepFolder Repetition for enclosed steps.

examPitfalls.title: Header assumptions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Subtracting one from every dimension count.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the returned count and actual table header structure.

examPitfalls.title: Ownership
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating every checkout as another user lock.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Green means you hold it; red means another user.

examPitfalls.title: ExplicitName
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating a renamed TestStepValue as a stable SUT ID.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Name editing and technical identification are separate.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A TestCase must dismiss an optional confirmation dialog exactly once if it is present, without looping or treating absence as failure. Which structure fits?

options.text: IF statement — check if the dialog is present; if true, click OK.
WHILE statement — repeat dismissal until the dialog disappears.
DO statement — always click OK at least once before checking.
Recovery Scenario — the dialog's appearance is treated as a test failure.

practiceQuiz.hint: Conditional action based on presence/absence of an element.
practiceQuiz.rationale: IF checks the condition and branches once; the scenario deliberately excludes looping and failure-driven handling.

optionExplanations.A: IF performs the optional action once under the stated condition.
optionExplanations.B: Looping is explicitly not requested here.
optionExplanations.C: It could try the absent dialog before checking.
optionExplanations.D: The expected optional state need not be turned into an error.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During an overnight unattended run, a TestCase fails and its Recovery Scenario cannot save it. The SUT is left in a messy state (logged in, cart full). You need the environment reset to a clean slate so the NEXT TestCase runs unaffected. Which mechanism does this?

options.text: Recovery Scenario — it recovers the current TestCase and continues it.
CleanUp Scenario — fires when the TestCase (and its Recovery) fails, resetting the SUT for the next TestCase.
A WHILE loop at the end of the TestCase.
It runs automatically after every TestCase whether it passed or failed.

practiceQuiz.hint: Fires after a failure to prepare a clean slate for the NEXT test.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Configured CleanUp attempts to restore the environment when Recovery is unsuccessful. It is not unconditional teardown or a guarantee that the next test passes.

optionExplanations.A: Recovery has already failed in the scenario.
optionExplanations.B: Configured CleanUp is the subsequent environment-reset attempt.
optionExplanations.C: An ordinary trailing loop may never be reached after failure.
optionExplanations.D: This is not always-run teardown for passing cases.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A confirmation message reads 'Order number: 48213' where the number is auto-generated and changes every run. You must verify the static text and also capture the number for later use. Which technique fits?

options.text: Verify with the full message hard-coded, including the number.
ActionMode Constraint to identify the message row.
ResultCount to count how many digits are in the number.
Dynamic Comparison with XBuffer: verify 'Order number: {XB[OrderNumber]}' — excludes the number from the match and buffers it.

practiceQuiz.hint: Static text + a changing part you also want to store = XBuffer.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Dynamic Comparison uses {XB[OrderNumber]} to verify the static portion ('Order number: ') while excluding the dynamic number from the comparison and storing it in the buffer 'OrderNumber' for later reuse. A hard-coded Verify would fail because the number changes every run.

optionExplanations.A: A changing ID makes the literal expected string unsuitable.
optionExplanations.B: Identification does not capture the dynamic substring.
optionExplanations.C: ResultCount measures matches, not the number of digits.
optionExplanations.D: Verify checks the static text and XB captures the changing part.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A generic product-card control definition intentionally matches all filtered product cards. You want to verify that there are exactly five matching nodes, independently of table-cell content. What is appropriate?

options.text: Verify the general control property .ResultCount==5 on that definition.
Use ActionMode Verify on each product card individually — 5 separate TestSteps.
Use ExplicitName on the 5th card and verify it exists.
Use TBox Set Buffer to read the page title and infer the count.

practiceQuiz.hint: Counting matching elements = one specific advanced feature.
practiceQuiz.rationale: General ResultCount counts matching current nodes. This differs from table ResultCount of constrained cells; existence of the fifth alone does not exclude a sixth.

optionExplanations.A: Counts matching nodes for the stated generic definition.
optionExplanations.B: Five separate checks need not exclude additional cards.
optionExplanations.C: The fifth can exist even when a sixth exists.
optionExplanations.D: Naming a buffer does not derive the page count.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A shopping cart has a dynamic number of items. You want to repeat the 'remove one row' TestSteps once per item — without a WHILE statement. You have already buffered the item count as {B[ActualCartNumber]}. How do you set this up?

options.text: Set the repetition in Project >> Settings >> Tbox.
Set the repetition on the ExecutionEntry in the ExecutionList.
Set the repetition count in the TestCase Properties.
Set Repetition on a TestStepFolder to {B[ActualCartNumber]}; each pass removes the current first data row after verifying its identity/state.

practiceQuiz.hint: Repetition lives in the TestStepFolder's Properties; the count can be a buffer.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Folder repetition accepts a dynamic expression. Deleting a row shifts later positions, so advancing an index after each deletion can skip items.

optionExplanations.A: Workspace settings are not this folder repeat count.
optionExplanations.B: Entry repetitions repeat execution entries, not this inner step group.
optionExplanations.C: The inner folder property is the appropriate scope.
optionExplanations.D: Repeats the step group and accounts for row shifts.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A table has exactly one row matching Product='Music 2' and Price='10.00'. Which ActionMode narrows to that row before operating its embedded Remove control?

options.text: Constraint — set Product='Music 2' and Price='*10.00*' as constraints to identify that specific row.
Select — pick the first row in the table.
Verify — compare each row's value to 'Music 2'.
WaitOn — wait until the row appears.

practiceQuiz.hint: Identify one specific item among similar ones, regardless of position.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Constraint narrows the parent-row search using the matching cell values. The scenario guarantees one match; the embedded control needs its own correct input action.

optionExplanations.A: Constraint narrows the row by the stated unique cell values.
optionExplanations.B: Picking the first physical row ignores its business identity.
optionExplanations.C: Comparing values alone does not establish the requested row-search constraint.
optionExplanations.D: Waiting does not specify the row selector.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Three similar buttons exist under stable parent 'action-panel', and their IDs change. Which approach establishes scoped identification without assuming the parent alone identifies the third button?

options.text: Identify by Properties using a wildcard on the ID.
Select the stable parent, then distinguish the child using additional stable properties or a justified index and validate uniqueness.
Use ExplicitName to give the element a fixed alias.
Rescan the module before every test run to capture the new ID.

practiceQuiz.hint: The parent is stable; the child is not — use the parent as the reference.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A parent scopes the search but does not alone distinguish similar children. Add a suitable discriminator and validate it against runtime states.

optionExplanations.A: A broad ID wildcard may still match all three buttons.
optionExplanations.B: Combines the stable scope with an actual child discriminator.
optionExplanations.C: A TestStepValue alias does not add a technical SUT identity.
optionExplanations.D: Repeated rescanning is not a stable identification strategy.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You intentionally need a bounded loop with additional polling steps until status becomes COMPLETED. It should skip the loop when the status is already complete. Which control structure fits?

options.text: DO statement — guarantees at least one poll before checking the condition.
IF statement — checks once and stops, regardless of the result.
WHILE statement — only polls if the status is not already 'COMPLETED'; may execute 0 times.
Recovery Scenario — polls on failure to handle the incomplete status.

practiceQuiz.hint: May not need to run at all = check condition first = WHILE.
practiceQuiz.rationale: WHILE checks before entering and may skip its loop. Set a bounded MaximumRepetitions; a simple single-property wait could instead use WaitOn.

optionExplanations.A: DO starts its loop before evaluating the condition.
optionExplanations.B: A single branch does not repeatedly perform the requested polling steps.
optionExplanations.C: Checks the condition before running a bounded loop.
optionExplanations.D: Recovery handles configured failures, not this expected control flow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When using the command {XB[Value]}, what is the meaning of the value inside the []?

options.text: The InnerText of the Control
The TestStep name
The value to be verified
The name of the Buffer

practiceQuiz.hint: XBuffer stores the excluded dynamic part somewhere.
practiceQuiz.rationale: In {XB[OrderNumber]}, the value inside the brackets is the NAME of the buffer where the excluded dynamic part of the string is stored for later reuse.

optionExplanations.A: The bracket content names the buffer, not InnerText.
optionExplanations.B: It does not specify a TestStep name.
optionExplanations.C: Static expected content belongs outside this dynamic placeholder.
optionExplanations.D: The name identifies where the captured substring is stored.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you define repetitions for TestSteps in a TestCase?

options.text: Change the number of repetitions in the properties of a TestStepFolder within the TestCase
Change the repetition setting in Project >> Settings >> Tbox
Set the repetition in the TestCase Properties
Set the repetition for the ExecutionEntry in the ExecutionList

practiceQuiz.rationale: Repetitions for TestSteps are defined in the PROPERTIES of a TestStepFolder within the TestCase (Attribute 'Repetition'). Not in Settings, TestCase Properties, or the ExecutionEntry.

optionExplanations.A: The TestStepFolder controls repetition of its enclosed steps.
optionExplanations.B: This is not the location of the inner folder count.
optionExplanations.C: The required scope is the TestStepFolder inside the case.
optionExplanations.D: This would affect outer execution rather than only enclosed steps.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Another user has checked out an existing Module, indicated by a red block. Which TWO statements describe your normal access while you edit a separate TestCase?

options.text: That object cannot be run in an Execution List
If it's a module, you may still add it to your TestCases
You cannot make any changes to that object
It means no one is working on that object

practiceQuiz.hint: Locked = can't edit, but a Module can still be used.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Another user owns the checkout. Its existing Module definition can be used while your changes require editing ownership; checkout color alone says nothing about execution success.

optionExplanations.A: Checkout color does not alone prohibit execution.
optionExplanations.B: Existing definitions may still be referenced from your editable case.
optionExplanations.C: The other owner prevents your editing this checked-out object.
optionExplanations.D: Red indicates another user owns the checkout.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the difference between a 'WHILE' and a 'DO' statement?

options.text: A 'WHILE' statement contains a loop, the 'DO' does not
In a 'DO' statement, the loop is executed at least once
The 'DO' statement is only a loop
A 'WHILE' statement must only be used in a Recovery Scenario

practiceQuiz.hint: One of them guarantees a minimum of one execution.
practiceQuiz.rationale: In a DO statement the loop is executed at least once (the condition is checked AFTER the first execution). A WHILE checks the condition first and may execute 0 times.

optionExplanations.A: Both WHILE and DO have Loop objects.
optionExplanations.B: DO enters its loop before checking; WHILE checks first.
optionExplanations.C: DO also has a Conditions object.
optionExplanations.D: WHILE is not restricted to Recovery.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the best definition of the ActionMode Constraint?

options.text: It's a type of ActionMode that allows you to interrupt the execution of the TestCase until the indicated property has the specified value
It's a type of ActionMode used for simple lists such as lists without sub-lists, or for a general verification of lists
It's a type of ActionMode used to identify one specific item in a list of similar items
It's a type of ActionMode that allows you to transfer values to the test object

practiceQuiz.hint: Constraint narrows a table search to one specific item.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ActionMode Constraint identifies one specific item in a list/table of similar items by constraining on cell values. Option A describes WaitOn, option B describes Select, and option D describes Input.

optionExplanations.A: This describes bounded waiting, not identification.
optionExplanations.B: Selection and list navigation differ from restricting the parent search.
optionExplanations.C: Constraint narrows a search using child values.

quickRecap.value: Green: yours; red: another user; white: newly created.
Configured failures; RetryLevel controls retry point.
Environment restoration after Recovery is unsuccessful.
Capture the variable substring during Verify.
Still needs a child discriminator and uniqueness check.
Stable properties or a unique wildcard combination.
Allows TestStepValue name editing; not universal identification.
Input writes; Verify checks the named buffer.
General nodes versus table constrained-cell counting.
Inspect headers before converting to data-only counts.
Folder count may be dynamic; deleting rows shifts indexes.
Narrows a parent-node search by child values.
